Noise Prediction and the appropriate computer program prepared at the U.S. Department of Transportation, Transportation Systems Center (Report: DOT-TSC-FHWA-72-1). The computer input and output are on file in the Illinois Department of Transportation, District 1 office.
This computer program was used to predict the 1990 traffic generated L10 noise levels by the improvement for the recommended design alternate. Predicted traffic generated L10 noise levels were computed for the seventy-seven (77) representative, probable noise sensitive locations. The tabulation of the predicted traffic generated noise levels (dBA) for each of the receivers is shown in Exhibit "13".
Other than the existing traffic on Lincoln Highway, there is one (1) other significant noise source. The Illinois Central Gulf Railroad tracks cross Lincoln Highway in the vicinity of the cross street known as Olympian Way.

All measurement of existing ambient noise did not screen, separate or adjust for noise that would be associated with the railroad traffic or any other significant noise sources in the area. Several of the noise sensitive locations and residential land uses involved with the proposed improvement are within 200 to 10,000 feet of the Illinois Central Gulf Railroad tracks and, therefore, are subject to significant volumes of noise daily from this source.
The noise level values (existing 1973, predicted 1990, and design year standards) were compared by the use of a tabulation. The entire tabulation is shown in Exhibit "13".
